title: Your MSI weekend
body:
The Mid-Season Invitational runs at the Daejeon Convention Center II (Hall 2), the first international League event ever held in Daejeon. Your tickets cover the Lower Bracket Final on Sat Jul 11 and the Grand Final on Sun Jul 12. Your Daejeon I-Hotel is ~130 m from the hall — a 2-minute walk — both days you stroll over.

What to bring:

  • Photo ID (passport) — tickets are name-tied and scanned at entry via the NOL World app
  • Bag no larger than 45.7 cm × 57 cm × 19 cm (~18" × 22" × 7.5"), must fit under your seat. DCC II has no bag check — oversized bags are turned away at the door with nowhere to leave them. The I-Hotel is 2 min away, so drop anything large before you walk over.
  • Outside food is allowed if sealed or in an appropriate container — saves money vs. arena concessions
  • Portable battery pack — phone needs to last all day for the NOL World ticket scan, live coverage, and GO Fest raids before/after

Prohibited (per the official Riot event policy): glass containers, cans, laser pens, air horns, banners or flags on poles, drones, selfie-sticks, laptops and tablets. Non-compliant items may be confiscated without return.

The merch queue is longest before the first match on Day 1 — arrive 60–90 min early if you want MSI merchandise. Day 2 line is shorter.

title: Getting to the arena
body:
From Seoul Station, the KTX reaches Daejeon in about 50 minutes (book on the Korail app or korail.com; use Seoul Station, not Suseo/SRT). From Daejeon Station, a taxi to the arena is ~20 min, {{fact:day-by-day-11-000}} (split two = {{fact:day-by-day-5-500}} each); the cheaper metro-plus-taxi combo runs ~25 min via Government Complex Daejeon (정부청사역). The arena is Daejeon Convention Center II (DCC II), 87 Expo-ro, Yuseong-gu — and your Daejeon I-Hotel (27-5 Expo-ro 123beon-gil) is ~130 m from it, a 2-minute walk, so you stroll to both matches and skip the post-match scramble entirely.

Monday Jul 13 — you don't ride straight back: You are staying both Saturday and Sunday nights at the I-Hotel, so there is no rush after the Grand Final. Monday is the Busan day trip — a slow Daejeon morning, then KTX south to Busan for the afternoon, and a Busan → Seoul train in the evening (full plan in the Monday day entry). Book the Daejeon → Busan (≈10:30) and Busan → Seoul (≈18:30) legs at letskorail.com (⚠ the day-of plan changed the exact Busan leg — see the Monday itinerary entry for what actually ran). Too wiped after MSI? Skip Busan and take a morning KTX Daejeon → Seoul instead.

While you're there, Sungsimdang (107 Expo-ro, near DCC II ⚠ verify hours) is Daejeon's legendary bakery — fried soboro and chive breads; queue moves fast. EXPO Science Park is adjacent to DCC II with open plazas, PokéStops, and gyms — useful for GO Fest raiding windows between matches. It's the former 1993 World's Fair site: a large open-air campus with wide walkways, gardens, and permanent science pavilions spread across roughly 1 km. Free to walk through; no entry fee for the public outdoor areas. Expect sun with little shade cover — hat and water matter here.

items.name: Hanbat Arboretum
items.kicker: Free green break near the base
items.body: A big public arboretum split into East and West Gardens plus an indoor Tropical Garden — one of Korea's largest urban botanical parks, ~1.5 km from DCC II (an easy taxi, or a walkable 20 min). East and Tropical Gardens run 09:00–18:00 (outdoor hours extend to 06:00–21:00 Apr–Sep) and close Mondays; the West Garden closes Tuesdays instead, so at least one half is open any day you go. Free entry, wide shaded paths, good PokéStop density — a solid sun-break between GO Fest raiding sessions. ⚠ Confirm same-day hours; seasonal closing times shift.

items.name: Yuseong Hot Springs Public Foot Bath (유성 온천 족욕체험장)
items.body: An open-air public foot bath using natural 40°C hot-spring water — four connected pools that hold ~200 people at once, free to use, open 08:00–22:00 daily. It sits in the Yuseong Hot Springs district (Bongmyeong-dong), a taxi ride from the EXPO/DCC area rather than a walk — worth it as a change of pace between matches, not a quick stroll. Bring a small towel; there's a wash station for your feet before you get in. ⚠ Confirm hours on the day.

items.name: Ppuri Park (뿌리공원)
items.body: A themed park built around filial piety and Korean family/clan names — sculpture gardens, a waterfront stage, a grass square and an observation deck across a wooded hillside in Jung-gu. Free entry; open 06:00–22:00 Mar–Oct and 07:00–21:00 Nov–Feb. It's on the far side of the city from the arena (Jung-gu, ~25–30 min by taxi from DCC II), so it's realistically a 'have a spare afternoon' pick rather than a between-matches one — pairs naturally with Daejeon O-World next door.

items.name: Daejeon O-World
items.body: A combined zoo, small amusement park (JoyLand) and flower garden on one site in Jung-gu, next to Ppuri Park. ⚠ Pricing runs by section — individual tickets {{fact:beyond-the-arena-12-000}} adult, or an all-inclusive day pass {{fact:beyond-the-arena-29-000}} adult (confirm current tiers before you go). Hours run roughly 10:30–18:00 (last admission 17:00), with later Saturday hours (to ≈22:00) May–October. Like Ppuri Park, it's a cross-town trip from the arena — a spare-afternoon option, not a between-matches one.

title: Beyond the arena — Daejeon food
intro: Sungsimdang and the near-base Yuseong-gu picks (Ossi Kalguksu, Cham-i-mat, Gobang Sikdang, Yakiniku Doryong) are covered in the Food & shopping tab. These are further-out, genuinely-different options if you have a gap between matches or want to see more of the city than the 130 m between the I-Hotel and DCC II.

items.name: Daejeon Jungang Market (대전중앙시장)
items.hours: General market ≈09:00–19:00; individual food stalls vary — ⚠ confirm same-day
items.how: From Daejeon Station: ~15–20 min walk north on Daejeon-ro, or a short taxi. Jungangno Station (Line 1) is closer still.
items.why: The region's biggest traditional market — 1,700+ stalls across dried-seafood, fish, herbal-medicine and 'delicacy' streets, plus an outdoor food alley (tteokbokki, hotteok, mung-bean pancakes, sundae).
items.crowd_tip: Natural pairing with a Daejeon Station KTX arrival or departure, since it's right there.

items.name: Poongnyeon Samgyetang (풍년삼계탕)
items.how: Near the Jungang Market side of town — a taxi from the I-Hotel/DCC area (~20–25 min).
items.why: Ginseng chicken soup made with Geumsan ginseng, the ingredient Daejeon's own samgyetang is known for — a long-running local pick, not a tourist chain.
items.crowd_tip: ⚠ Individual hours unconfirmed — call ahead or check Naver Map same-day.

items.name: Sutgol Won Naengmyeon (숯골원냉면)
items.how: ~15 min by taxi from the I-Hotel.
items.why: A fourth-generation Pyongyang-style naengmyeon house — chicken-broth cold buckwheat noodles from a family that fled south in the Korean War; a cooling lunch alternative to the near-base BBQ-heavy options.
items.crowd_tip: Closed on the 2nd and 4th Wednesdays of the month.

items.name: Daeseon Kalguksu Main Branch (대선칼국수 본점)
items.how: Dunsan-dong, near Daejeon City Hall Station — a taxi from the arena (~15–20 min).
items.why: A 70-plus-year knife-cut noodle institution in the Dunsan government-district area — a genuinely different neighbourhood from Yuseong if you want to see more of the city.
items.crowd_tip: Pairs with a Dunsan-dong shopping detour if you have a free afternoon.

items.name: Bongmyeong-dong eating street
items.how: ~5 min walk from the Yuseong Hot Springs foot bath.
items.why: A local eating street around the hot-springs district — seokgalbi (grilled short rib) and gukbap houses locals actually go to, well away from the arena's tourist gravity.
items.crowd_tip: ⚠ Specific restaurant names and hours weren't independently verified for this guide — treat this as 'walk the street and pick one,' not a booking, and check Naver Map for what's currently open.
